comparison.objective: Regrasp a memory chip across hands, orient its pins and notch, and seat it in a socket; candidate breaks tangs from already-installed inserts.
comparison.physical_skill: Reorientation, handover, and keyed pin insertion versus mandrel stabilization, controlled hammering, tool withdrawal, and loose-fragment recovery.
comparison.success_condition: Chip fully seated in the correctly keyed orientation and released versus four tang fractures with no coil/shell damage and all fragments contained.
comparison.reason: Both require precision alignment, but chip socketing tests orientation-sensitive insertion while the candidate tests contact-driven fracture and recovery.
